facts.raw_span: A 55-year-old man
history of coronary artery disease status post–bypass surgery
emphysema
chest pain, dyspnea, cough, night sweats, and a 20-pound unintentional weight loss
Physical examination was unremarkable
Laboratory studies, including a complete blood count and comprehensive metabolic profile, were within normal limits
a retrocardiac necrotic mediastinal mass measuring 1.2 × 8.6 × 10.7 cm
causing mass effect on the esophagus, left atrium, and pulmonary veins
Transbronchial needle aspiration of a right hilar mass showed benign bronchial cells
EUS-guided FNA of an oval, hypoechoic posterior mediastinal lesion (68 × 70 mm) obtained a core biopsy that demonstrated a spindle cell neoplasm with large nuclei and prominent nucleoli
Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CD117, DOG1, Cam5.2, and AE1/AE3
Somatic genetic analysis of cKIT and PDGFRA revealed no mutations, and germline testing was positive for NF1, suggesting wild-type GIST

concepts.why: The patient has a retrocardiac necrotic mediastinal mass with a spindle cell neoplasm and positive immunohistochemical staining for CD117, DOG1, Cam5.2, and AE1/AE3, suggesting a GIST.
The patient has a history of coronary artery disease status post–bypass surgery.
The patient has a history of emphysema.
The patient has multiple pulmonary nodules with FDG uptake on PET imaging, suggesting a possible neoplastic process.
The patient has a pleural-based lesion on the seventh rib with FDG uptake on PET imaging, suggesting a possible neoplastic process.
The mediastinal mass is causing mass effect on the esophagus, left atrium, and pulmonary veins, which is consistent with a mediastinal GIST.

rationales.F02: History of coronary artery disease status post-bypass surgery suggests C02.
rationales.F03: Emphysema is a known risk factor for C03 and may contribute to C04.
rationales.F07: Retrocardiac necrotic mediastinal mass is highly suggestive of C01 and C06.
rationales.F08: Mass effect on the esophagus, left atrium, and pulmonary veins is consistent with C01 and C06.
rationales.F09: Benign bronchial cells do not support C01 or C06.
rationales.F10: Spindle cell neoplasm with large nuclei and prominent nucleoli is characteristic of C01 and C06.
rationales.F11: Immunohistochemical staining positive for CD117, DOG1, Cam5.2, and AE1/AE3 supports C01 and C06.
rationales.F12: Somatic genetic analysis and germline testing results are consistent with wild-type GIST, supporting C01 and C06.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation of a retrocardiac necrotic mediastinal mass with spindle cell neoplasm and positive immunohistochemical staining for CD117, DOG1, Cam5.2, and AE1/AE3, along with the mass effect on the esophagus, left atrium, and pulmonary veins, strongly supports the diagnosis of a mediastinal GIST, which is a more specific diagnosis than a general GIST.
